facts.fact: At the 19 November 2025 closing, Minister Rose Pola Pricemou said Guinea is strengthening its regulatory framework with a new data-protection law, giving no stage, bill or date for it.

facts.fact: The CNT reported that on 20 June 2024 its commissions debated a bill to establish the Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel, an authority the 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law provides for, with members' designation and mandates still contested and plenary adoption pending.

facts.fact: ANSSI's summary states Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Condé, covering personal data processing by individuals, companies and public institutions; it gives no commencement statement and dates the law to 2016 only (document published 2016, year precision).

note: carried from dataprotectionlaw; no document opened

facts.fact: The National Assembly's text of Law L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and the protection of personal data carries the promulgation formula, with the law number and date left blank, and Part Two is a full personal data protection regime; it states no commencement date, and the record is dated only to July 2016 (document published date, month precision).
facts.system: Loi L/2016/037/AN relative à la cybersécurité et la protection des données à caractère personnel

facts.fact: The law defines an Autorité de Protection and gives it functions (declarations and authorisations, transfer approval, investigation, guidelines) but has processing declarations go to the competent authority 'designated by regulation' (Art. 5); it names no constituted body or appointed members (document published 2016-07).

facts.fact: The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Guinea ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 2018-07-31 and deposited its instrument on 2018-10-16.

facts.fact: Guinea's presidential decree D/2017/184/PRG/SGG of 26 July 2017 ratifies the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection signed at Malabo on 27 June 2014, effective from signature, following authorising law L/2017/023/AN of 16 June 2017.

note: The passage only says Guinea is still developing its AI policy or strategy; it states nothing on data protection law, treaty, authority or practice.

facts.fact: The ministry's secretary-general Nouhan Traore says Guinea has put in place the law on cybersecurity and protection of personal data.
